import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import t

# ============================================================
# MULTIPLE REGRESSION COEFFICIENT PLOT
# Risk Perception as the dependent variable
# Predictors: Knowledge, Concern, Symptoms, Trust
# ============================================================

# Reported regression results from the thesis
results = pd.DataFrame({
    "Predictor": ["Knowledge", "Concern", "Symptoms", "Trust"],
    "B": [-0.159, 0.396, 0.051, -0.001],
    "SE": [0.357, 0.067, 0.070, 0.061],
    "p_value": [0.657, 0.001, 0.469, 0.991]
})

# Residual degrees of freedom from the regression model
df_residual = 148

# 95% confidence level
alpha = 0.05

# Critical t-value
t_critical = t.ppf(1 - alpha / 2, df_residual)

# Calculate 95% confidence intervals
results["CI_lower"] = (
    results["B"] - t_critical * results["SE"]
)

results["CI_upper"] = (
    results["B"] + t_critical * results["SE"]
)

# Reverse order for a conventional forest/coefficient plot
results = results.iloc[::-1].reset_index(drop=True)

# ============================================================
# Plot
# ============================================================

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5.8))

y = np.arange(len(results))

# Error bars
xerr_lower = results["B"] - results["CI_lower"]
xerr_upper = results["CI_upper"] - results["B"]

ax.errorbar(
    results["B"],
    y,
    xerr=[xerr_lower, xerr_upper],
    fmt='o',
    markersize=8,
    capsize=5,
    linewidth=1.8
)

# Zero/reference line
ax.axvline(
    x=0,
    linestyle='--',
    linewidth=1.2
)

# Labels
ax.set_yticks(y)
ax.set_yticklabels(results["Predictor"])

ax.set_xlabel("Unstandardised regression coefficient (B)")
ax.set_ylabel("Predictor")

ax.set_title(
    "Regression Coefficients and 95% Confidence Intervals\n"
    "for Predictors of Risk Perception"
)

# Add p-values beside the estimates
for i, row in results.iterrows():

    if row["p_value"] < 0.001:
        p_text = "p < 0.001"
    else:
        p_text = f"p = {row['p_value']:.3f}"

    ax.text(
        row["CI_upper"] + 0.03,
        i,
        p_text,
        va="center",
        fontsize=10
    )

# Improve appearance
ax.grid(
    axis='x',
    linestyle=':',
    linewidth=0.7,
    alpha=0.6
)

ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout()

# Save high-resolution version for thesis
plt.savefig(
    "Figure_Regression_Coefficients_Risk_Perception.png",
    dpi=600,
    bbox_inches="tight"
)

plt.show()

# Display calculated confidence intervals
print(results)

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.api as sm

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# VARIABLES USED IN THE MULTIPLE REGRESSION MODEL
# ---------------------------------------------------------

variables = [
    "Risk_Perception",
    "Concern",
    "Knowledge",
    "Symptoms",
    "Trust"
]

# Keep only the variables required for the regression
reg_data = df[variables].copy()

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# LISTWISE DELETION
# Keep only respondents who have complete data
# across ALL variables in the regression model.
# ---------------------------------------------------------

reg_data = reg_data.dropna().reset_index(drop=True)

print("Regression sample size:", len(reg_data))

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1:
# Regress Risk Perception on the control variables:
# Knowledge, Symptoms and Trust
# ---------------------------------------------------------

X_controls = reg_data[["Knowledge", "Symptoms", "Trust"]]
X_controls = sm.add_constant(X_controls)

model_y = sm.OLS(
    reg_data["Risk_Perception"],
    X_controls
).fit()

# Residuals from Risk Perception after removing
# the effects of Knowledge, Symptoms and Trust
residual_y = model_y.resid

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2:
# Regress Concern on the same control variables
# ---------------------------------------------------------

model_x = sm.OLS(
    reg_data["Concern"],
    X_controls
).fit()

# Residuals from Concern after removing
# the effects of Knowledge, Symptoms and Trust
residual_x = model_x.resid

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3:
# Plot the residualised variables
# ---------------------------------------------------------

plt.figure(figsize=(9, 6))

plt.scatter(
    residual_x,
    residual_y,
    alpha=0.70,
    s=45
)

# Add constant for regression line
X_partial = sm.add_constant(residual_x)

partial_model = sm.OLS(
    residual_y,
    X_partial
).fit()

x_line = np.linspace(
    residual_x.min(),
    residual_x.max(),
    100
)

y_line = (
    partial_model.params.iloc[0]
    + partial_model.params.iloc[1] * x_line
)

plt.plot(
    x_line,
    y_line,
    linewidth=2
)

# Zero reference lines
plt.axhline(
    0,
    linestyle="--",
    linewidth=1
)

plt.axvline(
    0,
    linestyle="--",
    linewidth=1
)

plt.xlabel(
    "Concern residuals after controlling for Knowledge, Symptoms and Trust"
)

plt.ylabel(
    "Risk Perception residuals after controlling for Knowledge, Symptoms and Trust"
)

plt.title(
    "Partial Regression Plot of Concern and Risk Perception"
)

plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig(
    "Figure_Partial_Regression_Concern_Risk_Perception.png",
    dpi=600,
    bbox_inches="tight"
)

plt.show()
